content_json: {"term": "Atrial fibrillation", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "An irregular, often fast heart rhythm starting in the atria, with no distinct P waves.", "seen_in": "Older adults, hypertension, heart failure, hyperthyroidism, post-cardiac surgery.", "how_to_check": "ECG: irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm without P waves.", "related": ["Atrial flutter", "Stroke risk (CHA2DS2-VASc)"]}

{"term": "STEMI", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Heart attack with ST elevation on ECG, meaning a coronary artery is fully blocked.", "seen_in": "Middle-aged and older adults with smoking, diabetes, hypertension or high cholesterol.", "how_to_check": "ECG within minutes of arrival; troponin confirms heart muscle damage.", "related": ["NSTEMI", "Primary PCI"]}

{"term": "NSTEMI", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Heart attack without ST elevation; blockage is partial but heart muscle still dies.", "seen_in": "Similar patients to STEMI, often older with more background illness.", "how_to_check": "Troponin rise plus symptoms or ECG ischaemia without ST elevation.", "related": ["STEMI", "Unstable angina"]}

{"term": "Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "The heart pumps weakly (ejection fraction 40% or less), so fluid backs up into lungs and legs.", "seen_in": "After heart attacks, with long-standing hypertension or atrial fibrillation.", "how_to_check": "Echocardiogram measures ejection fraction; BNP supports the diagnosis.", "related": ["Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction", "Pulmonary oedema"]}

{"term": "Aortic stenosis", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Narrowing of the aortic valve that forces the heart to push harder with each beat.", "seen_in": "Older adults; younger patients with bicuspid valves or rheumatic disease.", "how_to_check": "Harsh ejection systolic murmur loudest at the upper right chest edge; echo confirms.", "related": ["Syncope", "Aortic regurgitation"]}

{"term": "Mitral regurgitation", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "The mitral valve leaks, letting blood flow backwards with each heartbeat.", "seen_in": "After heart attacks, with valve prolapse, rheumatic disease or endocarditis.", "how_to_check": "Pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the armpit; echo confirms.", "related": ["Mitral stenosis", "Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction"]}

{"term": "Infective endocarditis", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Infection of the heart valves, usually bacterial, that can destroy valve tissue.", "seen_in": "IV drug use, prosthetic valves, recent dental or surgical procedures.", "how_to_check": "Blood cultures before antibiotics, plus echo showing vegetations (Duke criteria).", "related": ["Septicaemia", "Osler nodes"]}

{"term": "Pericarditis", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Inflammation of the sac around the heart, causing sharp chest pain.", "seen_in": "Young adults, after viral illness, heart attack or cardiac procedures.", "how_to_check": "Pain worse lying flat and better sitting forward; ECG shows widespread saddle ST elevation.", "related": ["Pericardial effusion", "Cardiac tamponade"]}

{"term": "Cardiac tamponade", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Fluid in the pericardial sac squeezes the heart so it cannot fill.", "seen_in": "After trauma, heart procedures, cancer spread or severe pericarditis.", "how_to_check": "Beck's triad: low BP, raised neck veins, muffled heart sounds; urgent echo.", "related": ["Pulsus paradoxus", "Pericarditis"]}

{"term": "Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Inherited thickening of the heart muscle, often the septum, that can block outflow.", "seen_in": "Young athletes with fainting or family history of sudden death.", "how_to_check": "Echo shows asymmetric thickening; ECG often shows deep narrow Q waves.", "related": ["Dilated cardiomyopathy", "Sudden cardiac death in athletes"]}

{"term": "Dilated cardiomyopathy", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "The heart chambers stretch and weaken, usually from many causes including alcohol and viruses.", "seen_in": "Middle-aged adults with breathlessness, fatigue and leg swelling.", "how_to_check": "Echo shows enlarged chambers with poor pumping; look for a cause.", "related": ["Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy", "Alcohol and the heart"]}

{"term": "Atrial flutter", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "A fast regular atrial rhythm (~300/min) with a sawtooth baseline, often conducting 2:1.", "seen_in": "Similar patients to atrial fibrillation; after chest surgery or with lung disease.", "how_to_check": "ECG sawtooth flutter waves, best seen in the bottom ECG leads.", "related": ["Atrial fibrillation", "SVT"]}

{"term": "Supraventricular tachycardia", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "A sudden fast regular rhythm starting above the ventricles, often in young healthy hearts.", "seen_in": "Young adults with pounding episodes that start and stop abruptly.", "how_to_check": "ECG during the episode; vagal manoeuvres or adenosine can terminate it.", "related": ["Atrial flutter", "Wolff-Parkinson-White"]}

{"term": "Ventricular tachycardia", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "A fast wide-complex rhythm from the ventricles; unstable patients need urgent shock.", "seen_in": "After heart attacks, with cardiomyopathy or inherited rhythm disease.", "how_to_check": "Wide regular complexes on ECG; treat as VT until proven otherwise in a cardiac patient.", "related": ["Ventricular fibrillation", "Monomorphic vs polymorphic VT"]}

{"term": "Ventricular fibrillation", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Chaotic ventricular quivering with no pulse; immediate defibrillation saves lives.", "seen_in": "Cardiac arrest, acute heart attacks, drowning, electrocution.", "how_to_check": "No pulse plus chaotic ECG baseline: shock immediately, then CPR.", "related": ["Ventricular tachycardia", "Defibrillation vs cardioversion"]}

{"term": "Complete heart block", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "No electrical signal passes from atria to ventricles, so the ventricles beat slowly on their own.", "seen_in": "Older adults with conduction disease; after heart attacks or overdoses.", "how_to_check": "ECG shows P waves marching through independently of slow wide QRS complexes.", "related": ["Mobitz II", "Temporary pacing"]}

{"term": "First-degree AV block", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Every signal gets through but slowly (PR interval over 200 ms). Usually harmless.", "seen_in": "Athletes, older adults, or with beta-blockers and calcium-channel blockers.", "how_to_check": "ECG: PR interval over one large square with 1:1 conduction.", "related": ["Mobitz I", "Complete heart block"]}

{"term": "Mobitz type I (Wenckebach)", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "The PR interval lengthens each beat until one beat is dropped, then the cycle restarts.", "seen_in": "Inferior heart attacks, athletes, or with rate-slowing drugs.", "how_to_check": "ECG with grouped beating and lengthening PR before the dropped beat.", "related": ["Mobitz II", "First-degree AV block"]}

{"term": "Mobitz type II", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Sudden dropped beats with a constant PR interval; it can progress to complete block without warning.", "seen_in": "Disease of the conduction fibres below the AV node, often in older adults.", "how_to_check": "ECG: fixed PR interval with intermittent non-conducted P waves; needs pacing.", "related": ["Mobitz I (Wenckebach)", "Complete heart block"]}

{"term": "Aortic dissection", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "A tear in the aortic wall lets blood split its layers; type A is a surgical emergency.", "seen_in": "Hypertension, Marfan syndrome, pregnancy, cocaine use; sudden tearing chest pain to the back.", "how_to_check": "CT aorta urgently; unequal arm pressures or a new murmur support it.", "related": ["Abdominal aortic aneurysm", "Acute coronary syndrome"]}

{"term": "Abdominal aortic aneurysm", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "A swelling of the abdominal aorta over 3 cm that can rupture catastrophically.", "seen_in": "Older men who smoke; screening is offered at 65.", "how_to_check": "Pulsatile expansile mass; ultrasound measures it; rupture means emergency surgery.", "related": ["Aortic dissection", "AAA screening"]}

{"term": "Deep vein thrombosis", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "A clot in a deep leg (or arm) vein causing swelling and pain.", "seen_in": "Long flights, immobility, pregnancy, cancer, the pill, previous clots.", "how_to_check": "Wells score then D-dimer or Doppler ultrasound of the leg veins.", "related": ["Pulmonary embolism", "Wells score"]}

{"term": "Pulmonary embolism", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "A clot blocking lung arteries, ranging from breathlessness to instant collapse.", "seen_in": "After DVT, surgery, immobility, cancer or with no obvious cause.", "how_to_check": "CT pulmonary angiogram; tachycardia, low oxygen and pleuritic pain are typical.", "related": ["Deep vein thrombosis", "Thrombolysis"]}

{"term": "Hypertensive emergency", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Very high blood pressure WITH organ damage (chest pain, confusion, kidney injury).", "seen_in": "Missed tablets, kidney disease, pre-eclampsia, drug use.", "how_to_check": "Very high BP plus end-organ signs; lower in a controlled setting, never crash it.", "related": ["Hypertensive urgency", "Malignant hypertension"]}

{"term": "Orthostatic hypotension", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Blood pressure drops on standing, causing light-headedness or fainting.", "seen_in": "Older adults, dehydration, Parkinson's drugs, blood pressure tablets.", "how_to_check": "Lying then standing BP: a sustained 20/10 drop within 3 minutes confirms it.", "related": ["Vasovagal syncope", "Postural symptoms review"]}

{"term": "Vasovagal syncope", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "A common faint triggered by emotion, pain, heat or standing, with fast recovery.", "seen_in": "Teenagers and young adults; blood draws and hot crowded rooms.", "how_to_check": "Prodrome of nausea, sweating and tunnel vision, then brief loss of consciousness.", "related": ["Orthostatic hypotension", "Seizure vs syncope"]}

{"term": "Brugada syndrome", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Inherited sodium-channel disease causing coved ST elevation and risk of sudden death.", "seen_in": "Young men, often South-East Asian background, with fainting or family sudden death.", "how_to_check": "Type 1 Brugada ECG pattern (coved ST elevation in V1-V3), sometimes only with fever.", "related": ["Long QT syndrome", "Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy"]}

{"term": "Long QT syndrome", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Delayed heart repolarisation that can trigger twisting VT (torsades), often during exercise or fright.", "seen_in": "Children and young adults with fainting during swimming or loud alarms.", "how_to_check": "Corrected QT over 470 ms (men) or 480 ms (women); avoid QT-prolonging drugs.", "related": ["Brugada syndrome", "Torsades de pointes"]}

{"term": "Wolff-Parkinson-White", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "An extra electrical pathway that can drive dangerously fast rhythms if AF develops.", "seen_in": "Young people with palpitations; found incidentally on ECG.", "how_to_check": "Short PR interval with a slurred upstroke (delta wave) on resting ECG.", "related": ["Supraventricular tachycardia", "Atrial fibrillation with WPW"]}

{"term": "Takotsubo cardiomyopathy", "specialty": "Cardiology", "meaning": "Sudden stress-triggered heart failure that mimics a heart attack but recovers.", "seen_in": "Older women after severe emotional or physical stress.", "how_to_check": "ECG and troponin like a heart attack, but coronaries are clean and the apex balloons.", "related": ["STEMI", "Myocarditis"]}

{"term": "Asthma", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Reversible airway narrowing causing wheeze, cough and chest tightness, often at night.", "seen_in": "Children and young adults, with eczema, hay fever or family history.", "how_to_check": "Variable peak flow diary or spirometry reversibility; raised FeNO or eosinophils support it.", "related": ["COPD", "Inhaler technique"]}

{"term": "COPD", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Fixed airflow obstruction from smoking or biomass smoke, with chronic breathlessness.", "seen_in": "Long-term smokers over 40; GOLD stages guide treatment.", "how_to_check": "Spirometry with FEV1/FVC below 0.7 after bronchodilator confirms it.", "related": ["Asthma", "Cor pulmonale"]}

{"term": "Community-acquired pneumonia", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Lung infection caught outside hospital, from mild to life-threatening.", "seen_in": "Older adults, the very young, smokers and the immunosuppressed.", "how_to_check": "Fever, cough, focal crackles plus new shadowing on chest X-ray; CURB-65 scores severity.", "related": ["Hospital-acquired pneumonia", "CURB-65"]}

{"term": "Pneumothorax", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Air in the pleural space partially collapsing the lung.", "seen_in": "Tall thin young men spontaneously; COPD, trauma or procedures secondarily.", "how_to_check": "Sudden pleuritic pain with reduced breath sounds; erect chest X-ray confirms.", "related": ["Tension pneumothorax", "Chest drain"]}

{"term": "Tension pneumothorax", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Trapped air under pressure shifts the mediastinum and crushes venous return; fatal if missed.", "seen_in": "Trauma, ventilated patients, or a simple pneumothorax under positive pressure.", "how_to_check": "Hypotension, tracheal deviation away, distended neck veins: decompress before X-ray.", "related": ["Pneumothorax", "Needle decompression"]}

{"term": "Pleural effusion", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Fluid in the pleural space compressing the lung.", "seen_in": "Heart failure (transudate), infection, cancer or pulmonary embolism (exudate).", "how_to_check": "Stony dullness with reduced breath sounds; tap it (Light's criteria sort the cause).", "related": ["Empyema", "Light's criteria"]}

{"term": "Bronchiectasis", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Permanently widened airways that trap mucus and invite repeated infections.", "seen_in": "After severe childhood infections, cystic fibrosis, immune defects.", "how_to_check": "Daily productive cough with exacerbations; high-resolution CT shows signet-ring airways.", "related": ["COPD", "Postural drainage"]}

{"term": "Interstitial lung disease", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "A family of scarring lung disorders causing progressive dry cough and breathlessness.", "seen_in": "Rheumatoid arthritis, bird or mould exposure, certain drugs.", "how_to_check": "Fine end-inspiratory crackles with restrictive spirometry; HRCT defines the pattern.", "related": ["Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis", "Sarcoidosis"]}

{"term": "Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Unexplained progressive lung scarring with a poor prognosis.", "seen_in": "Men over 60, often smokers.", "how_to_check": "Velcro crackles at the bases with a UIP pattern on HRCT; antifibrotics slow decline.", "related": ["Interstitial lung disease", "Clubbing"]}

{"term": "Sarcoidosis", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Granulomas in lungs, nodes, skin and eyes; often burns out on its own.", "seen_in": "Young adults, more common with African ancestry.", "how_to_check": "Hilar nodes on X-ray with raised ACE; biopsy shows non-caseating granulomas.", "related": ["Tuberculosis", "Erythema nodosum"]}

{"term": "Pulmonary tuberculosis", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Airborne mycobacterial lung infection; a global killer that needs months of treatment.", "seen_in": "Crowding, HIV, diabetes, homelessness, migration from endemic areas.", "how_to_check": "Chronic cough, night sweats and weight loss; sputum NAAT/culture confirms.", "related": ["Latent TB", "Directly observed therapy"]}

{"term": "Non-small cell lung cancer", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "The commonest lung cancer group (adeno and squamous), often found late.", "seen_in": "Smokers over 50; radon and asbestos exposure add risk.", "how_to_check": "Persistent cough, haemoptysis or weight loss; CT then tissue diagnosis and staging.", "related": ["Small cell lung cancer", "Lung cancer screening (low-dose CT)"]}

{"term": "Mesothelioma", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Cancer of the pleura strongly tied to asbestos, appearing decades later.", "seen_in": "Shipyard, construction and insulation workers.", "how_to_check": "Breathlessness with a rind-like pleural mass on CT; biopsy confirms.", "related": ["Asbestos exposure", "Pleural plaques"]}

{"term": "Cor pulmonale", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Right heart failure caused by chronic lung disease.", "seen_in": "Severe COPD, pulmonary hypertension, recurrent clots.", "how_to_check": "Raised neck veins and ankle swelling in a breathless lung patient; echo confirms.", "related": ["COPD", "Right heart failure"]}

{"term": "Acute respiratory distress syndrome", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Sudden widespread lung inflammation flooding alveoli; ICU-level illness.", "seen_in": "Sepsis, pneumonia, aspiration, major trauma, pancreatitis.", "how_to_check": "Refractory low oxygen with bilateral X-ray opacities not explained by fluid overload.", "related": ["Pulmonary oedema", "Lung-protective ventilation"]}

{"term": "Obstructive sleep apnoea", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Repeated airway collapse in sleep causing snoring, apnoeas and daytime sleepiness.", "seen_in": "Obesity, thick neck, hypertension, truck drivers at risk on the road.", "how_to_check": "STOP-Bang screening then sleep study; CPAP transforms symptoms.", "related": ["Snoring vs apnoea", "CPAP"]}

{"term": "Cystic fibrosis", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Inherited chloride-channel disease clogging lungs and pancreas from childhood.", "seen_in": "Northern European ancestry; newborn screening catches most cases.", "how_to_check": "Recurrent chest infections with salty sweat; sweat chloride or genetics confirms.", "related": ["Bronchiectasis", "Pancreatic insufficiency"]}

{"term": "Bronchiolitis", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Viral small-airway infection of infants, peaking in winter.", "seen_in": "Babies under 1 year, RSV season, nursery contact.", "how_to_check": "Crackles, wheeze and poor feeding in a snotty infant; treatment is oxygen and fluids.", "related": ["Viral wheeze", "RSV"]}

{"term": "Croup", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Viral upper-airway swelling giving a barking cough and stridor in toddlers.", "seen_in": "Children 6 months to 3 years, autumn evenings.", "how_to_check": "Seal-like bark with low-grade fever; single-dose dexamethasone settles most.", "related": ["Epiglottitis", "Stridor"]}

{"term": "Epiglottitis", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Swollen epiglottis threatening the airway; a do-not-touch emergency in children.", "seen_in": "Unvaccinated children (Hib), adults with sore throat and drooling.", "how_to_check": "Toxic child sitting forward drooling with muffled voice: secure the airway first.", "related": ["Croup", "Drooling child protocol"]}

{"term": "Foreign body aspiration", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Inhaled object (often a peanut) blocking a child's airway.", "seen_in": "Toddlers eating while running around or laughing.", "how_to_check": "Sudden choking, unilateral wheeze later; bronchoscopy removes it.", "related": ["Croup", "Back blows and chest thrusts"]}

{"term": "Haemoptysis", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Coughing blood, from streaks to life-threatening volumes.", "seen_in": "Bronchiectasis, TB, cancer, pulmonary embolism.", "how_to_check": "Quantify it, secure the airway if massive, then CT and bronchoscopy hunt the source.", "related": ["Epistaxis vs haemoptysis", "Massive haemoptysis protocol"]}

{"term": "Clubbing", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Bulbous fingertips with lost nail-bed angle, signalling chronic disease.", "seen_in": "Lung cancer, fibrosis, bronchiectasis, cyanotic heart disease, IBD.", "how_to_check": "Schamroth window test at the bedside; always look for the underlying cause.", "related": ["Hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy", "Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis"]}

{"term": "Stridor", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Harsh inspiratory noise meaning upper-airway narrowing.", "seen_in": "Croup, epiglottitis, inhaled objects, anaphylaxis.", "how_to_check": "Inspiratory vs expiratory timing localises it; never agitate a toxic child.", "related": ["Wheeze", "Croup"]}

{"term": "Wheeze", "specialty": "Respiratory", "meaning": "Musical expiratory sound of narrowed small airways.", "seen_in": "Asthma, COPD, bronchiolitis, heart failure, inhaled objects.", "how_to_check": "Polyphonic and diffuse suggests asthma; fixed single wheeze needs imaging.", "related": ["Stridor", "Asthma"]}

{"term": "Ischaemic stroke", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "A blocked brain artery kills tissue within minutes; thrombolysis and thrombectomy windows are short.", "seen_in": "Older adults with AF, hypertension, diabetes or smoking.", "how_to_check": "FAST face-arm-speech signs; immediate CT head to exclude bleeding, then reperfusion.", "related": ["TIA", "Thrombolysis window"]}

{"term": "Transient ischaemic attack", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Stroke symptoms resolving within 24 hours (usually minutes); a warning, not a reprieve.", "seen_in": "Same vascular patients; ABCD2 scores early risk.", "how_to_check": "Same-day specialist review, brain and carotid imaging, secondary prevention.", "related": ["Ischaemic stroke", "ABCD2 score"]}

{"term": "Subarachnoid haemorrhage", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Bleed into the CSF space, classically a thunderclap headache like never before.", "seen_in": "Middle age, smoking, hypertension, family aneurysms.", "how_to_check": "CT head immediately; lumbar puncture for xanthochromia if CT is negative.", "related": ["Thunderclap headache", "Nimodipine"]}

{"term": "Subdural haematoma", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Blood between dura and brain, often after minor trauma in older or anticoagulated patients.", "seen_in": "Falls, alcohol use, warfarin or DOACs; fluctuating consciousness.", "how_to_check": "CT head shows crescent collection; burr holes or craniotomy drain it.", "related": ["Extradural haematoma", "Falls in older adults"]}

{"term": "Extradural haematoma", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Arterial bleed (often middle meningeal) after head injury with a lucid interval.", "seen_in": "Young men in road accidents, assaults and contact sports.", "how_to_check": "Brief recovery then rapid decline; lens-shaped CT collection needs urgent surgery.", "related": ["Subdural haematoma", "Lucid interval"]}

{"term": "Migraine", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Recurrent throbbing headache with nausea and light/sound sensitivity, sometimes with aura.", "seen_in": "Young women, family history, hormonal and stress triggers.", "how_to_check": "Clinical diagnosis by pattern; red flags (thunderclap, new over 50) need imaging.", "related": ["Tension headache", "Triptans"]}

{"term": "Tension headache", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Band-like pressing headache from muscle tension and stress; the commonest kind.", "seen_in": "Desk workers, students, poor sleep and posture.", "how_to_check": "Bilateral pressure without nausea; posture, sleep and simple analgesia treat it.", "related": ["Migraine", "Medication-overuse headache"]}

{"term": "Cluster headache", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Excruciating one-sided eye pain with tearing and restlessness, in bouts.", "seen_in": "Young men who smoke; attacks often wake them at night.", "how_to_check": "Strictly unilateral with autonomic features; high-flow oxygen aborts attacks.", "related": ["Migraine", "Trigeminal neuralgia"]}

{"term": "Giant cell arteritis", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Large-vessel vasculitis threatening sudden blindness; steroids cannot wait.", "seen_in": "Over-50s with new headache, jaw pain on chewing or visual symptoms.", "how_to_check": "Raised ESR/CRP supports it; temporal artery biopsy confirms; start steroids now.", "related": ["Polymyalgia rheumatica", "Amaurosis fugax"]}

{"term": "Bell's palsy", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Sudden one-sided facial weakness from facial nerve inflammation; most recover.", "seen_in": "After viral illness, diabetes, pregnancy.", "how_to_check": "Entire half of the face including the forehead; steroids early, protect the eye.", "related": ["Stroke (face sparing forehead)", "Ramsay Hunt syndrome"]}

{"term": "Trigeminal neuralgia", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Lightning-bolt facial pain triggered by touch, eating or cold wind.", "seen_in": "Older adults; younger onset suggests multiple sclerosis.", "how_to_check": "Brief electric shocks in trigeminal zones; carbamazepine is first line.", "related": ["Cluster headache", "Dental pain"]}

{"term": "Tonic-clonic seizure", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Generalised convulsions with stiffening then jerking and a drowsy aftermath.", "seen_in": "Epilepsy, alcohol withdrawal, low sodium, missed tablets.", "how_to_check": "Witnessed rhythmic jerking with tongue biting and post-ictal sleep.", "related": ["Absence seizure", "Status epilepticus"]}

{"term": "Absence seizure", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Brief staring spells in schoolchildren, dozens a day, mistaken for daydreaming.", "seen_in": "Children 4-10 years, often outgrown by teens.", "how_to_check": "Hyperventilation in clinic can trigger one; EEG shows 3-per-second spike-wave.", "related": ["Tonic-clonic seizure", "Ethosuximide"]}

{"term": "Status epilepticus", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "A seizure lasting over 5 minutes or repeated without waking; brain injury looms.", "seen_in": "Epilepsy with missed doses, alcohol withdrawal, infections.", "how_to_check": "Clock it early: benzodiazepine first, then load levetiracetam or phenytoin.", "related": ["Tonic-clonic seizure", "Buccal midazolam"]}

{"term": "Parkinson's disease", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Dopamine loss causing slow movement, resting tremor, rigidity and shuffling.", "seen_in": "Over 60s; men slightly more; family history in a minority.", "how_to_check": "Bradykinesia plus tremor or rigidity; levodopa response supports it.", "related": ["Essential tremor", "Drug-induced parkinsonism"]}

{"term": "Essential tremor", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Action tremor of the hands (and head/voice) that runs in families.", "seen_in": "Any age, worse with anxiety, caffeine and movement; alcohol may briefly help.", "how_to_check": "Bilateral postural tremor without parkinsonism; propranolol or primidone help.", "related": ["Parkinson's disease", "Physiological tremor"]}

{"term": "Multiple sclerosis", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Immune attacks stripping myelin cause scattered relapses: vision, limbs, bladder.", "seen_in": "Young women, northern latitudes, after infections like EBV.", "how_to_check": "Lesions separated in space and time on MRI; lumbar puncture oligoclonal bands.", "related": ["Clinically isolated syndrome", "Optic neuritis"]}

{"term": "Guillain-Barre syndrome", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Post-infectious nerve attack causing ascending weakness that can stop breathing.", "seen_in": "Weeks after diarrhoea (Campylobacter) or flu.", "how_to_check": "Ascending flaccid weakness with lost reflexes; monitor breathing, give IVIG.", "related": ["Myasthenia gravis", "Tick paralysis"]}

{"term": "Myasthenia gravis", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Antibodies block the neuromuscular junction, so muscles fatigue with use.", "seen_in": "Young women and older men; drooping eyelids and double vision first.", "how_to_check": "Fatigable weakness improving with rest; acetylcholine-receptor antibodies.", "related": ["Lambert-Eaton syndrome", "Myasthenic crisis"]}

{"term": "Motor neurone disease", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Progressive loss of upper and lower motor neurones; mixed signs in one limb.", "seen_in": "Middle-aged and older adults; usually sporadic.", "how_to_check": "Wasting with brisk reflexes and fasciculations; EMG confirms, riluzole slows.", "related": ["Multifocal motor neuropathy", "Bulbar palsy"]}

{"term": "Alzheimer's disease", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Commonest dementia: gradual short-term memory loss with brain shrinkage.", "seen_in": "Over 65s, family history, Down's syndrome, vascular risks.", "how_to_check": "Insidious memory decline affecting function; exclude reversible causes first.", "related": ["Vascular dementia", "Mild cognitive impairment"]}

{"term": "Vascular dementia", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Stepwise cognitive decline from small strokes and white-matter disease.", "seen_in": "Hypertension, diabetes, smoking, previous strokes.", "how_to_check": "Stepwise rather than gradual course; MRI shows small-vessel burden.", "related": ["Alzheimer's disease", "Binswanger disease"]}

{"term": "Delirium", "specialty": "Neurology", "meaning": "Acute fluctuating confusion with inattention; a medical emergency in disguise.", "seen_in": "Older inpatients with infection, dehydration, new drugs or constipation.", "how_to_check": "4AT screening; hunt and treat the trigger, reorient, review drugs.", "related": ["Dementia", "4AT test"]}
